bottleneck: Many staple crops are polyploid — wheat has six genome copies — so editing a trait requires modifying every homoeolog simultaneously. Incomplete edits produce chimeric plants with unpredictable phenotypes, and delivering editors into plant cells through rigid cell walls remains inefficient. Regeneration of edited cells into whole plants is genotype-dependent and often fails in elite varieties, meaning the cultivars farmers actually grow are the hardest to engineer.
current_state: Multiplex CRISPR works in model polyploids, but elite crop varieties remain recalcitrant. Transformation and regeneration, not editing chemistry, are the practical bottlenecks limiting deployment.
title: Polyploid crop genomes resist complete editing
why_it_blocks: The crops that feed billions are the hardest to edit. Until delivery and regeneration work in elite varieties, gene editing's agricultural promise stays limited to easy model plants while food security demands more.
